description: Canonical-CBOR sign/verify golden vector exercising the C1 HashMap-ordering fix. The payload is a CBOR map with deliberately unsorted insertion order (zebra, apple, mango, agent, action); canonical_cbor() re-sorts the keys lexicographically before signing, so the signature is stable regardless of input iteration order. Cross-language verifiers (Python, Go) verify the signature over the canonical_cbor_hex bytes — they MUST NOT re-serialize the map themselves, since that would re-introduce ordering nondeterminism. Verifies identically in Rust, Python, and Go.
encoding: RFC 8949 §4.2.2 deterministic CBOR (core determinism): map keys sorted by length then bytewise. The canonical_cbor_hex field below is the exact byte sequence that was signed; verifiers treat it as opaque payload bytes.
payload_utf8_note: The payload is binary CBOR (not valid UTF-8 text); use payload_hex.
notes: Generated by aumos-trust-core::canonical::canonical_cbor + ed25519-dalek. The C1 fix (sort_value in canonical.rs) is what makes this signature reproducible: without the sort, HashMap iteration order would vary the CBOR bytes and the signature would be non-deterministic. The Rust unit test in rust/trust-core/src/canonical.rs::determinism_hashmap_vs_btreemap_same_output locks the determinism property; this vector locks the concrete bytes + signature for cross-language conformance.
